verdict: The revision fixes every mechanical blocker the first implementation-fit pass raised, and I verified the ones that can be verified: the section-8 DDL (partial unique index, four guarded ALTERs, five new tables) executes cleanly on the system SQLite 3.51.0 against a hand-built v2 schema, the MAX(version)+1 insert plus retired-row delete works under the (group_id, version) PK, and NULL group_uid rows coexist under the partial index; C1/R2/section 8 now agree that a genesis carries whatever group_dek row it inserts; MAX_VALUE = MAX_MSG - 4 KiB with a MAX_MSG + 64 KiB bound on all three readers is arithmetically coherent with the existing max-size e2e test (a Secret reply of MAX_VALUE + ~20 B still fits an old Go client's 4 MiB bound, one cap-sized SealedVersion fits an Export page or a StageVersions message); Hello gains a body on the new ALPN; StageVersions is open to any registered identity with the stage keyed by submitter; SyncStatus.rejected gives apply_bunker_secret (which already holds Arc<Replica> and calls status()) a data path for ChainRejected; GroupInfo.chain_perms and AddIdentity.revive are compatible under protocol.md section 8's unknown-field rule. What is still not implementable as written: (1) the two-phase lock discipline is specified as an algorithm but has no entry point in Bunker::handle/handle_raw/accept, no owner or runtime for the retried server-side rotate, no restart resume of needs_rotation, and would double-audit SubmitEpoch; (2) the phase plan ships RemoveIdentity orphaning in phase 1 while recovery author / epoch submit are phase 3 and db grant / recover, kept until phase 3, corrupt the group_acl projection or no-op on a v3 database; (3) replica genesis trust (expect_genesis without --tofu) cannot be seeded before db migrate-epochs mints the hashes, and every later CreateGroup has the same problem. The rest are one-sentence fixes.

unfixed_prior.prior_title: S8's out-of-lock verification does not fit Bunker::handle; server-authored rotates re-encrypt whole groups under the global lock (implfit-A MAJOR, implfit-B minor, authz-B MAJOR)
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: The revision specifies WHAT happens (D13 two-step revocation, 6.1 server-side steps 1-3, S8 'blocking thread', 6.3 'outside the lock, retried with backoff until it lands') but not HOW it enters the code, and the code shape makes the how load-bearing. Bunker::handle (src/server.rs:197-227) is `pub fn handle(&self, remote, req) -> Response`, takes the single std Mutex<Store> before dispatch and holds it for the whole call; ProtocolHandler::accept calls handle_raw inline (src/server.rs:1021); the same sync handle is called directly from more than twenty non-async #[test]s in server.rs (e.g. remove_identity_rotates_all_readable_groups at 2191) and from tests/e2e.rs:2559. Nothing in the spec says handle special-cases SubmitEpoch / RemoveIdentity / legacy shrink Grant before taking the lock, that accept awaits a spawn_blocking for step 2, or how dispatch(store: &mut Store) can release and re-take a lock it does not own. The rotating half ('retried with backoff until it lands') needs a task owner: Inner has no runtime handle, JoinSet or worker channel, and a tokio::spawn from inside handle panics in the existing non-async unit tests that section 13 says will cover 'RemoveIdentity -> carry per group under the lock, Put fenced, rotate lands afterwards'. No startup step resumes needs_rotation = 1 groups (grep: 'startup' appears only for the R5 sets), so a crash between the carry commit and the rotate commit leaves the group Put-fenced until an admin happens to rotate, contradicting D13's 'until it lands'. Step 1's snapshot is 'the head record and the list of retained rows with their (dek_gen, nonce)', but step 2's S5 trial decryption needs the staged ciphertext and the current ciphertext of every row, which live behind the same mutex, so the snapshot must copy 2x retained ciphertext into memory under the lock. Finally handle unconditionally appends store.audit(remote, req.op(), &req.target(), outcome) after dispatch (server.rs:213), while 6.1 step 3 appends 'submit-epoch' inside the install transaction via audit_in: two submit-epoch rows per accepted submit, with different targets.
unfixed_prior.fix: Add to 6.1/S8: (a) handle matches SubmitEpoch, RemoveIdentity and legacy shrink Grant before locking and routes them to Bunker::submit_epoch(&self, remote, ...) / Bunker::revoke(...) which take and drop the lock themselves; accept awaits tokio::task::spawn_blocking for those variants (handle_raw stays sync for everything else). (b) Inner gains `rotations: tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedSender<PendingRotate>` plus a worker task started by a new `Bunker::spawn_rotator(&self) -> JoinHandle` that serveloop calls once (tests call `Bunker::run_pending_rotations()` synchronously); the worker scans `secret_group WHERE needs_rotation = 1` at start and after every carry. (c) Step 1's snapshot includes the staged rows and the current rows' ciphertext. (d) The generic post-dispatch audit is skipped for SubmitEpoch (audit_in inside the transaction is the only row) and the background rotate audits 'rotate-dek' with the original wire requester carried in PendingRotate.

unfixed_prior.prior_title: No bootstrap for a fresh v3 database: init never specified (implfit-A MAJOR)
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: Section 11 now specifies `init --operational-key --backup-id [--mode] [--admin-id]` writing operational_ed25519 / backup_ed25519 / epoch_mode / schema_version=3 / epochs_migrated=1 / role, and the KeyRole change. But the three places that decide 'is this database initialized and is this the right key' still key on the age recipient and the spec does not say they move: Store::is_initialized() (src/store.rs:259) tests meta 'operational_pubkey'; Bunker::new (src/server.rs:64-88) reads 'operational_pubkey' and 'backup_pubkey' and compares the age recipient; migrate() (src/store.rs:180-195) stamps `role` from 'operational_pubkey'. A literal implementation of section 11 produces a v3 database with none of those keys, so `serve` fails 'database is not initialized (run `init` first)' and `db grant`/`init` guards misfire. The prior fix text explicitly asked for 'is_initialized() keys on operational_ed25519'.
unfixed_prior.fix: One sentence in 11 or 12.3: is_initialized() and Bunker::new key on meta.operational_ed25519 (and backup_ed25519, epoch_mode); migrate()'s role stamping is unchanged for v2 and init writes role itself for v3; the age keys 'operational_pubkey'/'backup_pubkey' are left in meta after db migrate-epochs for snapshot forensics only and never consulted.

unfixed_prior.prior_title: Upgrade order assumes replicas serve their last mirror during the ALPN-fail window (implfit-B MAJOR) - fixed by the transitional read path, but the fix contradicts 12.3
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: Section 10 now says a v3 replica 'keeps the age read path (agebridge + local dek_wrap rows) for a group that has no group_epoch rows yet'. Section 12 step 3 says 'ReplicaInner::age_identity becomes the replica's Ed25519 scalar' and section 8 says agebridge.rs is dropped 'in a later v4 cleanup'. Replica::get (src/replica.rs:161-186) unwraps with `&self.inner.age_identity` (age::x25519::Identity) and the shared server::read_secret (src/server.rs:875-899) takes `dek_identity: &age::x25519::Identity`; ReplicaServer::dispatch passes `&inner.age_identity`. If age_identity becomes the Ed25519 scalar there is no age identity left for the transitional path, so test 13(5) 'no serving gap' cannot pass; if it stays age, the ElGamal path has no scalar field. The revision fixed the ordering finding by adding a path that the same document removes.
unfixed_prior.fix: State in 10 and 12.3: ReplicaInner holds both `age_identity` (agebridge::identity_from_secret, transitional) and `elgamal_scalar` (Zeroizing, from the same SecretKey); Replica::get and read_secret dispatch on whether the group has a head record (group_epoch row) and use the age path otherwise; both the field and agebridge.rs go in v4.

unfixed_prior.prior_title: Pin protection is void for the k8s operator's emptyDir mirror (implfit-B MAJOR) - fixed by the pins Secret, but only the load half has an API
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: Section 10 names `ReplicaBuilder::pins(...)` for loading the operator-owned `<release>-bunker-pins` Secret at boot and says it is 'written on every accepted head', but nothing returns pins to the operator: SyncStatus (src/replica.rs:69-74: connected, last_synced, groups, authoritative) gains only `rejected`, no `Replica::pins()` is listed, and ReplicaEvent carries no head data. The only new event, ChainAccepted{group}, is worded in P1 as the rejection-clearing event ('The rejection clears, with ReplicaEvent::ChainAccepted{group}, when a head for the group is accepted'), not as a per-head event, and a carry that changes no secret emits no SecretChanged (apply_group_state only emits per-secret changes, src/replica.rs:880-900). A pins Secret written only on the events that exist lags the true head; after a pod restart a rewound authoritative node whose head is at or above the lagging pin is accepted, which is the case the Secret was introduced to close.
unfixed_prior.fix: Add `Replica::pins(&self) -> Vec<GroupPin{name, group_uid, genesis_hash, head_epoch, head_hash}>` (or `SyncStatus.pins`) and define ChainAccepted{group, head_epoch, head_hash} as emitted on EVERY accepted head (rejection clearing is a consequence, not the trigger); operator/src/events.rs writes the pins Secret on it (RBAC already allows secrets create/patch, charts rbac.yaml:16-17) and test 13(6) asserts the Secret advances on a carry that changes no secret.

findings.section: 16 (phases 1-3) vs 6.3 RemoveIdentity, 6.4, 11 (db grant / recover removal), src/main.rs db_grant and Recover
findings.title: The phase-1+2 release can orphan a group (RemoveIdentity, G2 exception) but ships no recovery path, and the legacy db grant / recover it keeps until phase 3 corrupt or no-op on a v3 database
findings.detail: Phase 1 ships server-authored revocations for RemoveIdentity, which 6.3 says 'may orphan a group (G2 exception), whose recovery is 6.4'. Phase 3 ships `recovery author`, `client epoch export|submit` and 'removal of db grant/recover'. So for the whole phase-1+2 release the only recovery for an orphaned (or rogue-admin-hijacked, S10 is phase 1 too) group is the offline flow that does not exist yet, and e2e test 13(7) cannot be written. Meanwhile the legacy commands still exist and are wrong on a migrated database: db_grant's non-read branch (src/main.rs:575-580) calls store.set_perms directly on group_acl, which section 8 makes 'a projection of the head record, rebuilt inside every apply transaction' - the row is honoured by authorize_group on the authoritative node, never mirrored by any replica (P5 uses the verified head), and silently erased at the next accepted record; its read branch (src/main.rs:509-530) errors on the empty dek_wrap table ('DEK v.. has no operational wrap'); `recover` (src/main.rs:841-865) finds zero backup wraps in dek_wrap, prints 're-wrapped 0 DEK(s)' and rewrites meta.operational_pubkey (the archived age key) via apply_recovery - a misleading no-op during an operational-key incident.
findings.fix: Either move `recovery author`, `client epoch export|submit`, `db reset-pin` and the removal of `db grant`/`recover` into the phase-1+2 release (they share epoch.rs with everything else in phase 1), or have phase 1 make `db grant` and `recover` refuse with 'signed epochs: use recovery author' when meta.epochs_migrated is set and state in 16 that orphaned groups are unrecoverable until phase 3. Say which in the phase table and in 6.3.

findings.section: 10 P2 (expect_genesis / --tofu) vs 12 step 4 and 6.3 CreateGroup; 13 e2e (3) and (5)
findings.title: Replica genesis trust cannot be seeded before migration mints the hashes, and every later CreateGroup produces a genesis no replica is configured to accept
findings.detail: P2: a genesis 'whose keys or hash differ from the configuration is rejected (unpinned-genesis). Without configuration and without a pin, genesis is trust-on-first-use only when --tofu is set; otherwise rejected', and test 13(3) has 'an unpinned replica without --tofu' reject a genesis while presumably holding expect_keys for the test bunker - so expect_keys alone does not admit a genesis; a per-name expect_genesis entry or --tofu is required. Section 12 step 4 upgrades and configures the operator and standalone replicas ('seeded by bunker.expect*') BEFORE `db migrate-epochs` (step 2) draws every group_uid and genesis hash, so the hashes cannot be in the chart or the flags at upgrade time; the first sync after migration is rejected for every group unless --tofu is set, and the operator's BunkerSecrets stay Ready=False beyond the maintenance window. The same applies forever after: `CreateGroup` (6.3) mints a genesis server-side, and a replica granted read on the new group rejects it until someone edits bunker.expectGenesis and restarts the pod (or runs --tofu permanently, which nullifies P2). The emptyDir + pins Secret design does not help here: there is no pin for a name never mirrored. Test 13(5) 'no serving gap' and criterion 6 (operator works unchanged after upgrading the image) depend on which reading is intended.
findings.fix: Define the admission rule explicitly. Recommended: expect_keys match (authority, backup, mode) admits an unlisted genesis and pins it, audited `sync-genesis-keys`; expect_genesis[name] is an optional stricter pin for names the operator cares about; --tofu is only for a replica with no expect_keys at all. Update 13(3) to 'unpinned replica with wrong/absent expect_keys and no --tofu -> rejected', and have db migrate-epochs print each group's genesis hash for operators who want the strict pin. If the strict reading is intended instead, 12.4 must add a second operator/replica rollout after migration and 6.3 must document that every CreateGroup needs a chart change.

findings.section: 10 (Hello{have}, C1 re-mirror branch, P1/P3) vs Store::drop_group_local and group_epoch's FK
findings.title: What a replica lists in Hello.have for a pinned-but-dropped group is unspecified, and the natural answer (its pin) breaks C1's re-mirror path and the chain-wide R2/R5 checks
findings.detail: drop_group_local (src/store.rs:1190-1196) executes `DELETE FROM secret_group WHERE name = ?1`; the new group_epoch table references secret_group(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, so after a P3 drop or a manifest-absence drop the replica keeps group_pin{head_epoch, head_hash} and nothing else. Section 10 says the server ships 'the records after the replica's have_epoch (the whole chain for a name it did not list)' and C1 accepts a genesis 'if the pin's genesis_hash equals the record's hash (a re-mirror after a drop)'. If the replica builds `have` from group_pin (the only state it still has), the server sends only records > head_epoch: the replica can check prev == pin.head_hash but cannot evaluate R2 ('differs from every commit seen in the chain') or R5 ('no c0 seen earlier in the chain') and never exercises C1's re-mirror branch; the chain would have to be re-fetched with FetchGroup{have_epoch: 0} anyway.
findings.fix: State in 10: `have` is derived from groups with a mirrored head (a group_epoch row), never from group_pin alone; a pinned-but-dropped group is unlisted, receives the whole chain, must satisfy C1 against pin.genesis_hash and P1 (the chain passes through pin.{head_epoch, head_hash}), and rebuilds its per-group R5 sets from genesis.

findings.section: 12 step 3 and 3.8 (PRAGMA secure_delete, VACUUM) vs Store::open
findings.title: secure_delete is a per-connection pragma, not a database property, so 'from now on' at migration time does nothing for later opens; VACUUM must stay outside the per-group transactions
findings.detail: Verified with the system sqlite3 3.51.0: `PRAGMA secure_delete=ON; VACUUM;` in one session, then reopening the file reports the compiled default (2 = FAST on this build), i.e. the setting is not persisted. Store::open (src/store.rs:212-245) sets journal_mode and foreign_keys on every open and is the only place a persistent policy can live; 12 step 3 phrases it as a one-time migration side effect. Also verified: `BEGIN; VACUUM;` fails with 'cannot VACUUM from within a transaction', which is fine for the step-3 ordering as written but must not be folded into the step-2 per-group transaction by an implementer.
findings.fix: Move the pragma to Store::open/open_in_memory for both roles ('PRAGMA secure_delete = ON' next to foreign_keys) and say in 12.3 that migrate-epochs runs VACUUM after all per-group transactions have committed and outside any transaction.

findings.section: 6.4 operational-key replacement vs 6.3 CreateGroup and Bunker::new
findings.title: During the two-key window it is unstated which key mints new genesis records and which key meta must match at startup; as written, groups created during the window inherit the suspected-compromised authority and the window can never close
findings.detail: 6.4: `serve --operational-key new.key --previous-operational-key old.key`, 'when [no head] names the old authority, meta.operational_ed25519 is advanced'. 6.3: CreateGroup mints genesis with authority from the configured value; S2: for genesis authority equals 'the server's configured values'. If meta.operational_ed25519 stays = old until the end of the window, every CreateGroup during the window (routine in the k8s setup) names the old key and needs its own recovery, so 'GroupStatus shows which groups still name the old authority' never reaches none while groups are created. Separately, Bunker::new today refuses to start when the supplied operational key differs from the recorded one (src/server.rs:71-78); with two keys the spec does not say which of them must equal meta.operational_ed25519, so the startup check cannot be written.
findings.fix: State: on a start with --previous-operational-key, meta.operational_ed25519 := new and meta.operational_ed25519_previous := old (audited `authority-rotated` at that point); genesis and S2's 'configured value' mean the new key; S2 for recovery accepts either; the previous key is dropped (meta row deleted) at the first restart after GroupStatus shows no head naming it.

findings.section: 5 S10 FreezeGroup vs 6.3 RemoveIdentity ('never blocked') and the rotating half; 6.4 step 0-1
findings.title: A freeze does not stop server-authored records, so RemoveIdentity or the pending authority rotate can move the head under an in-flight offline recovery
findings.detail: S10 refuses non-recovery SubmitEpoch, legacy Grant and Put while frozen; 6.4 step 0-1 freezes precisely so the exported head (prev of the recovery) stays stable during the hours-long offline signing. But 6.3 makes RemoveIdentity 'never blocked' and it authors an authority carry per affected group (a new head), and the rotating half 'retried with backoff until it lands' is not a SubmitEpoch either. A service admin who freezes the group and then, naturally, removes the rogue admin's identity while the bundle is being signed makes the recovery answer EpochConflict (C2) and restarts the ceremony; a RemoveIdentity carry that landed just before the freeze leaves a pending authority rotate that lands during it with the same effect. FreezeGroup, the carry and the rotate are all phase-1 server code, so the interaction must be decided now.
findings.fix: State in S10/6.3: while a group is frozen the rotating half is deferred (needs_rotation stays set; the recovery must be a rotate anyway, R6), and RemoveIdentity on a frozen group still lands its carry but `client freeze-group` and GroupStatus warn that any exported bundle must be re-exported; alternatively refuse RemoveIdentity on a frozen group unless --force and document it as the one exception to 'never blocked'.

findings.title: S9's per-author 30 s limit on accepted non-rotating records also throttles an admin's own consecutive edits, which the TUI issues one keystroke at a time
findings.detail: S9: 'at most one accepted non-rotating record per author per group per 30 s'. 6.2 describes add-reader and bit edits as one record each, and 11 maps every TUI ACL-pane keystroke (r/w/a on a row, n to add) to one carry or rewrap. An admin who adds carol and then clears bob's write bit, or toggles w twice, gets `Failed{"S9: rate"}` on the second record and an audit row; a CLI script granting three readers in a loop fails on the second. The rule was introduced to make head-churn by a kick target costlier than the kicker's rebase, and a limit that also hits the honest author's normal workflow will be worked around (batching in the client) or disabled.
findings.fix: Either scope S9 to records whose ACL delta touches only the author's own row (the churn shape from 6.1 step 8) or allow a small burst (e.g. 5 per 30 s per author per group); have the CLI/TUI batch a multi-edit into one record where possible and retry once after the window otherwise. State the chosen shape in S9 and in 11.
